_doc: Shipped defaults for tools.json -- the limits, folders, word lists and result wording of tools.py (AGENTS.md Rule 0). Edit tools.json, not this file: tools.py falls back to the value here, with a log line, for any key in tools.json that is missing or invalid. Templates are Python str.format strings and may only use the {fields} their default here uses. Kept in tools.py on purpose, because brain.py, brain.json and multistep.py read them back: the 'Error: ' prefix, '(no output)', '(empty file)', find_files' 'Found N match(es)' and 'No files matching' lines, the task tools' 'Added:', 'Marked done:' and 'Removed:' results, and recall's 'I don't have anything remembered' (brain.json evidence.found_nothing_patterns).

open_application._doc: store_search_timeout_seconds: how long the Start Menu app search may take. not_found points at find_files on purpose: a bare 'couldn't find it' was relayed to Chuen as the file not existing (2026-10-26).
open_application.not_found: No application called '{app_name}' (tried a direct launch and a Start Menu search). This only looks at installed apps, not at files. If '{app_name}' is a document, call find_files(query='{app_name}') before telling Chuen anything about whether it exists.

find_files._doc: search_folders: folders under the home folder searched when no location is given; each is known by its name in lower case. onedrive_prefix: home-folder entries starting with this (any case) are OneDrive roots whose top-level folders are searched too; one whose name collides with a search folder is filed as '<onedrive_prefix> <name>'. skip_dir_names: folder names (lower case) never descended into. filler_words: words dropped from a natural-language query before every remaining word must appear in the file name -- the model passes his phrasing ('my japan flight pdf'), the file is 'Japan_flight.pdf'.
find_files.empty_query: give me something to search for.
find_files.unknown_location: Don't know a location called '{location}'. Known folders: {known}.
find_files.no_folders: couldn't find any of the usual folders to search.
find_files.more: ...and {more} more, narrow the query to see them.

calculate._doc: round_digits: float results are rounded to this many decimal places, so binary noise (9.9 - 9.11 = 0.7900000000000009) never gets read aloud.

time._doc: strftime formats. twelve_hour is said alongside the 24-hour one, leading zero dropped, so the model never converts by hand.

weather._doc: url: {location} is URL-quoted, {format} is format below. One clean line, not wttr.in's ANSI-art report.

news._doc: One flowing sentence, not a bulleted list: a bulleted result was much less reliable (the model claimed no news over real headlines).

voice.no_key: No Inworld API key is configured, so replies fall back to the local Windows voice (pyttsx3), not a neural voice.
voice.neural: Neural voice: '{voice}' via Inworld's '{model}' model. Falls back to the local Windows voice only if that fails.

brain_location._doc: positive_percent is worked out from instincts.json activation.min_positives_per_negative.
brain_location.save_auto: when useful facts appear in conversation
brain_location.saving: I save personal facts {save}. I use the last {turns} conversation turns.
brain_location.vault: Vault lookup is {state}, limited to {chars} characters per lookup.
brain_location.learning: Learning is {state}: {confirmed} confirmed lessons, {candidates} candidates. Activation requires {confirmations} accepted fixes and at least {positive_percent}% positive feedback on that lesson.
brain_location.learning_limits: Learning changes tool selection and supported read-only retrieval intent; it cannot grant new action permissions or rewrite code.
brain_location.invalid_settings: The last settings edit was invalid: {error}. Keeping the last valid settings.
brain_location.mirrored: That memory also gets mirrored (read-only, one-way) into the Obsidian vault at {vault}. The mirror is not my conversation store. Vault notes are searchable on demand when enabled; validated routing lessons are also stored there.
brain_location.no_vault: The Obsidian vault isn't currently reachable, so nothing is mirrored there right now.

clean_temp.nothing: Nothing to clean -- no temp files old enough to remove.

facts._doc: recall() matches a key worded differently from the saved one. spelling: [variant, canonical] pairs folded first. ignore_words carry no meaning in a key. A query word of prefix_length+ letters sharing that prefix with a fact word scores prefix_score (an exact word scores 1); the key counts key_weight times the value. closest_shown: matches listed when there's no single best; known_shown: keys listed when nothing matches.
facts.not_found: I don't have anything remembered for '{key}'. Facts I do have are filed under: {known}.

skills.unknown: No skill named '{name}'. Use list_skills to see what's available.

tasks._doc: framing: how add_task trims the model copying his framing into the task text ('remind me there is a robotics meeting' -> 'robotics meeting', 2026-11-03). It trims the model's argument, never his words; each slot is optional except asks, and a phrase's words may be split by any spacing. The deadline window for OVERDUE marks is reminders.json tasks.due_soon_hours.
tasks.ambiguous_due: Not added yet: "{due}" is ambiguous. Ask Chuen: {question} Then call add_task again with the day he means.
tasks.no_match: No single open task matched "{task}" -- either it isn't there or more than one matched. Say the exact task name.

calendar._doc: What check_calendar says. A tool result is the one thing the model treats as ground truth, so 'no calendar' lives here (2026-11-04: it asserted an empty calendar with none to read).
calendar.not_connected: No calendar is connected to Denisse, so nothing about his calendar can be seen or checked -- not for {day}, not at all. Tell him plainly you can't see his calendar; don't say it's empty or free. His reminders (list_tasks) are the nearest thing you can read.
calendar.no_reader: a calendar is configured but no calendar reader is installed. Tell him this failed.
